title: Optimize: Recs Workbench — wireframes & grooming notes (draft)
content:
Context and goal:
We need a lightweight Workbench view inside Console Optimize where engineers and platform owners can preview automated recommendations (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles), tune thresholds, and push a recommended configuration to a rollout policy. This doc is a combination of quick wireframe notes, user flows, edge-cases, and initial grooming backlog for the next sprint.

High-level product principles for this surface:
- Non-invasive: recommendations should be suggestions, not automatic changes. Clear CTA for apply vs save-for-later.
- Explainability: each recommendation must include: why, expected cost/latency delta, confidence score, and conservative vs aggressive option variants.
- Safety-first: always validate quantization with a fallback model, show eval risk for quality-sensitive routes.
- Observable outcomes: show an estimated impact and link to post-rollout evaluation (perf + quality).

Primary personas:
- ML Platform Engineer (wants predictable throughput gains with low risk)
- Product Engineer (needs quick cost win without regressions)
- SRE (concerned about latency p90/p99 regressions)

Wireframe sketches (textual):
1) Recs Workbench landing (left rail + main panel)
- Left rail: saved recommendation sets, filters (by model family, service/route, rec type: batching/caching/quantization), search.
- Main header: Selected route/model, dataset preview link, traffic profile snapshot (QPS, p50/p95/p99, median seq len). Small explainer: how recommendations were generated.
- Top controls: Time window selector (last 24h/7d/14d), baseline vs projected toggle, simulation mode checkbox (apply to a simulation environment only).

2) Recommendation list (main column)
- Each rec is a card with micro-UI:
  - Title: short human-readable ("Suggest: dynamic batching -> max_batch_size=8, timeout=12ms")
  - Tagline: one-line expected outcome ("~20% lower per-token cost, +10ms p95")
  - Confidence pill: High/Medium/Low (color-coded) and numeric score (0-100)
  - Impact bar: horizontal bars for cost delta / latency delta / quality risk (colored)
  - Action buttons: [Simulate] [Save draft] [Apply to Canary] [Dismiss]
  - Expand area shows: rationale, input traces used, mean seq length buckets affected, related tickets, and quick toggles to choose conservative/aggressive knobs.

3) Detail pane (right side when card expanded)
- Two tabs: "Simulate" and "Safety"
- Simulate tab: expectation table (baseline vs projected), token-cost calc assumptions, per-region impact if routed, and a timeline chart (simulated QPS vs latency).
- Safety tab: unit test of prompts (quick eval on small default prompt set), fallback policy (which model to revert to), pre-check list (memory fit, kv-cache invalidation note).

4) Quick-edit modal for quantization
- Options: target bitwidth (8/4/llm.int4), calibration strategy (static/dynamic), quant library (default/new).
- Show estimated memory saving and expected perf delta.
- Warning flags: "Quantization may affect output fluency for long-context prompts" with link to quality regression playbook.

5) Batching UI micro-interaction
- Slider for max_batch_size with sample throughput curve that updates live.
- Timeout input (ms).
- Checkbox: "Enable dynamic batching for prefix-shared requests only".
- Visual indicator for cold-start risk when batch size is high and p95 latency must be under X ms.

6) Caching UI
- Toggle for prefix caching and KV caching.
- For prefix caching show: cache hit estimate %, estimated token-savings/week, and expiration settings.
- For KV caching: per-user vs per-session policy with storage footprint estimation.

User flows (happy path):
- Team lead opens route -> sees 4 suggestions -> expands first (batching) -> runs simulate (choose 7-day window) -> confirms no p99 regressions -> selects "Apply to Canary" -> chooses 10% traffic -> confirms rollout policy -> clicks apply -> workbench creates OPT-521 canary rollout and adds a note.

Edge cases / open questions:
- Multi-model pipelines: how do we present compounding effects when batching or quantizing one stage affects downstream latency? (Action: add pipeline-level simulation ticket OPT-437).
- Conflicting recs: user could get a batching suggestion that increases latency and a caching suggestion that reduces it. Priority rules needed: combine, rank by net latency+cost.
- Access control: who can apply vs who can only save drafts? Integrate with org RBAC.
- Data sensitivity: caching prefixes for PII. Need KMS/HSM labels on cache storage.
- Metrics lag: recommendation accuracy depends on telemetry freshness. Display data freshness timestamp.

Acceptance criteria for MLP (first ship):
- Workbench loads for a given route/model and displays at least three recs types (batching, caching, quantization).
- Simulate runs and returns expected cost/latency deltas within 10% of offline estimator.
- "Apply to Canary" creates a rollout draft with chosen knobs and links back to the original rec.
- Recs are dismissible and can be re-enabled from left rail.
- Audit log shows who applied what and when.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets and priorities):
- OPT-521: Implement Recs Workbench skeleton + left rail (P0)
- OPT-522: Recommendation card component + impact bars + expand details (P0)
- OPT-523: Simulation service contract and UI integration (P0)
- OPT-524: Quick quantization modal + validation checks (P1)
- OPT-525: Batching slider and throughput curve preview component (P1)
- OPT-526: Caching estimator + expiration UX (P1)
- OPT-527: RBAC checks & "apply" gating (P1)
- OPT-528: Pipeline-level compounding simulation (spike, P2)
- OPT-529: Post-rollout eval hook + perf/quality diff dashboard link (P1)
- Opt-UI: accessibility pass + keyboard flows (P2)

Telemetry & success metrics to track post-launch:
- % of recommendations simulated before applied
- Acceptance rate (applied/candidate) and rollback rate within 7 days
- Mean cost-per-token delta for applied recs (downward target)
- p99 latency regression rate tied to recs (should be <1% of rollouts)

Design constraints and notes for implementation team:
- Keep simulation fast (<6s for a typical route) by sampling and using cached baseline metrics.
- Use existing rollout API to create canary policies; UI only submits config, backend handles safety checks.
- Reuse cost-estimator library from Optimize backend; add lightweight deterministic simulator for UI preview.
- Mobile/responsive: Workbench primarily desktop-first.

Unresolved discussion points for next sync (agenda items):
1) How precise must the confidence score be and where does it come from? (analytics vs ML model)
2) Should dismissed recommendations be permanently hidden or resurfaced after X days?
3) What default prompt set for quick unit-evals for quantization safety?
4) How to display region-specific differences when routing rules are active?

TODOs (short-term):
- Priya: prototype card components in Figma using the impact bar metaphors (due 2025-02-17)
- Derek: spike on in-UI simulation latency reduction (OPT-523) (due 2025-02-21)
- Jin: draft RBAC policy for who can apply recommendations (due 2025-02-24)
- Marisol: write rollout acceptance language and update audit schema (OPT-521) (due 2025-02-19)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory; focus feedback on: clarity of action flows, missing safety checks, and data required for accurate simulations.
- Add comments inline in Figma and leave tickets for any UI-to-backend contract needs.

End of doc.
